checklist.what: Moorage — a dock (the tar-dark boat waits here | FOOTPRINT STAMPED 2026-08-01 (coordinator ruling, stilt waterfront footprints): the extent-4 disc put 64 m2 of walkable pad on the river and walk_water_audit measured 607 samples of it standing on open water — the town's worst walk-on-water record. tools/landing_footprint.py finds NO all-landed rectangle of 1.5 m2 anywhere inside the disc; 3% of it is landed. The two rects stamped here are the moorage's REAL built landing, measured on lf_stage_moorage (largest all-landed rect 6.8 x 1.8) and lf_stage_moorage_w (1.0 x 3.0), both built by locksfoot_build.py and both largely OUTSIDE the old disc — which is exactly what that file's own comment says: 'everything the moorage WORKS with has to stand off it'. WIDTH 1.80 m, not the 2.00 m the landing rule asks for: walk_e_moorage__lock-five_l0 slopes down to 0.67 across the pier's east 0.14 m, and honouring it at full width would have put the deck 0.595 m under the pad — inside the 0.60 m rule by 5 mm, which the planking's own jitter would have spent. | THE WEST LINK IS BUILT 2026-08-05, and the FOURTH rect is it. The 2026-08-01 pier joined the staging to `pos`; it did not join the WEST STORE rect [70.9,71.9,26.2,29.2] to anything, because waterfront_landings' connective rect runs 2.0 m about `pos` and the west store is not in that column — so the one rect that ruling had already found to be an island stayed one, and it is a ONE-WAY PIT: walk_pad_tenant-shack (1.92..2.04) hangs 0.72 m over its 1.199 deck, which is a legal 0.79 m step DOWN and 0.16 m past STEP_UP coming back, with the pad's own slab 20 mm inside the body's blocking window over that floor ([1.85, 2.50]). The Chapter Two playtest agent stepped down at step 75 of run-20260805-054441 and was still on it at step 120 — 46 of 120 steps, filing five reports about pillars. tools/moorage_westlink.py measures the gap (2.46 m of open water; both banks lf_planking at top 1.199; the body window 1.85..2.50 CLEAR) and plank-links it; these FOUR rects are measured 228/228 all-landed over that deck. THE SHAPE IS THE MEASUREMENT: a 0.15 m occupancy scan of the body window (1.85..2.50 over a 1.199 floor) finds exactly two obstructions and they are at OPPOSITE CORNERS — the stair's t03/t04 undersides fill x 74.30..75.50 for y <= 28.50 (north-EAST), and lf_railings, the west store's own guard, fills a diagonal x 71.00..71.45 for y 28.95..29.55 (south-WEST). Of the six l2 treads only those two have an underside in that window at all: t02's is 2.55 (clears by 50 mm) and t05's TOP is 1.66 (under it). The only single rectangle that misses both corners is 0.15 m wide, which is why this is three overlapping rects and not one.)
